A pocket of more stable air and light winds between Tropical Storm
Saudel and a secondary monsoon trough has moved over the Marianas.
This will allow for potentially heavy island effect showers and
isolated thunderstorms to develop over Guam, Tinian, and Saipan, with
the highest rainfall over Guam. This will be additionally fueled by
evapotranspiration from already saturated soils. The only 
potentially limiting factor would be if upper level cirrus bands from
Saudel drift over the islands. By Friday night, winds will begin to 
pick up for all islands with scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms moving into Tinian and Saipan as Saudel passes just 
northeast. The monsoon tail of Saudel will bring moisture to all 
islands and any thunderstorms will have the potential for gusty winds
and heavy rainfall. However, tropical storm conditions are not 
expected at this time. This monsoon tail has the potential to sit 
over the Marianas for much of the rest of the forecast period but 
this remains uncertain at this time. Residents of the Marianas should
continue to monitor the forecast. 

Marine...
Light to gentle winds tonight will be easing by Friday morning. 
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet will begin to increase Friday ahead of 
current Tropical Storm Saudel, particularly for Tinian and Saipan. 
Seas are currently expected to reach as high as 9 feet for Tinian and
Saipan by Friday night, so near hazardous conditions to small craft.
As soon as Friday night, wetter conditions with elevated winds, 
locally heavy showers, and isolated thunderstorms can also be 
expected. In terms of coastal surf, there is a moderate risk of rip 
currents along north- and west-facing reefs. A moderate risk of rip 
currents will develop for east-facing reefs Friday. This will likely 
become a high risk of rip currents for east-facing reefs Friday 
night and surf may reach near high surf advisory criteria, 
particularly for Tinian and Saipan as Tropical Storm Saudel moves 
closer to the Marianas. A moderate risk of lightning will also begin 
Friday and persist through the week. This situation will continue to 
be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Saudel (17W) continues to move northwest, away from 
Chuuk State. At 5 PM ChST, the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) 
position was 11.9N 150.9E. Based on the latest satellite imagery, the
center continues to drift slightly northwestward, and is currently 
about 425 miles east-southeast of Guam and 410 miles east-southeast 
of Saipan. Saudel is moving northwest at 17 mph and is expected to 
maintain this general course with a decrease in forward speed through
Sunday. This general track passes over or near Agrihan in the far 
Northern Marianas Saturday and Saturday night. We will continue to 
monitor Saudel as it moves northwestward towards the far northern 
Marianas.

For further information on Tropical Storm Saudel, please refer to the
Local Statement issued by the National Weather Service under WMO
header WTPQ81 PGUM, the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM, the
Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center
under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW, and the Significant Tropical Weather
Advisory under WMO head ABPW10 PGTW. 

Eastern Micronesia...
Light to moderate winds will prevail through the period across 
eastern Micronesia. The monsoon trough will dominate the weather 
across all of Micronesia for the entire period, an unusual regime 
caused by the strong El Nino. Pohnpei will have isolated showers 
through Friday, then scattered showers through Tuesday. Kosrae will 
have isolated tonight, then scattered to numerous through Monday, 
then isolated again Tuesday. Majuro will have scattered to numerous 
through the entire period. Basically, it will be a wet week.

For hazards, Kosrae has a high surf advisory which is expected to end
late tonight. Otherwise, seas will be 5 to 7 feet through Saturday
night and Pohnpei and Kosrae, then 4 to 6 feet. At Majuro, they will
be 4 to 6 feet through the period.

Western Micronesia...
An intensifying monsoon surge along the southern peripheries of a 
developing trough axis stretching from TS Saudel westward, is 
expected to enhance a secondary embedded monsoon disturbance that 
will bring intensely heavy showers and persistently fresh to strong 
westerlies to much of western Micronesia the next several days. As
such, sea conditions are expected to become hazardous to small craft
in Palau waters beginning Friday, so a Small Craft Advisory has been
issued for that time. Intense showers and thunderstorms are expected
to peak at Yap tonight and Friday, to then taper down slowly 
thereafter. Meanwhile at Palau, the aforementioned secondary 
disturbance will develop quickly, to bring peak shower and thunder 
potentials on Friday and Friday night, which may drag into the
